Verdict: Absorb nothing new yet; run the frozen three-task real cohort first, while deferring the SCM pilot, Smartlog graphs, and Scion/Piper/Sapling architectures.
Evidence: Practical usefulness and economics are unverified beyond synthetic fixtures, Northstar explicitly bars adding process without observed friction, and external SCMs solve unshown scale needs.
Risk: A three-task cohort may be too small or unrepresentative to expose multi-task overlap friction, potentially masking whether ready SCM workflow primitives (exact review identity, dirty-state preservation) are actually needed.

Own verdict: Absorb no new mechanisms now; run the frozen three-task matched cohort before new frameworks/features. Fact: usefulness and full-effort economics remain unverified. Inference: testing existing skills-centered workflows offers more decision value than adding process.
Gemini review: Agree on cohort-first sequencing because synthetic checks cannot establish accepted real work or savings; qualify SCM deferral—observed interruption/overlap failures could justify testing the already-designed safeguards, not adopting another SCM.
Next: Run the first frozen matched task with unchanged acceptance criteria and independent review; record acceptance, total effort, and owner rescue; complete all three before reassessing additions.
Risk: Three tasks may miss overlap/interruption friction; absence of failures would not establish that SCM safeguards are unnecessary.
